messages:
marco-cs: customer on enterprise reports rerank returning 422 for some requests and scores sometimes come back as strings. started after they upgraded both clients. unhappy because their scoring pipeline fails. they provided request samples and logs.
tess: can you paste the SDK call they used and which versions for python/ts? any request-id?
marco-cs: they sent two snippets. TS client: 
```ts
import Redwood from 'redwood-sdk'
const client = new Redwood({apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY})
const res = await client.rerank({
  model: 'rerank-alpha',
  query: 'best cameras',
  candidates: ['doc1', 'doc2']
})
console.log(res.scores)
```
node package versions: redwood-js@1.2.2 -> 1.2.3 they upgraded.
Python snippet: 
```py
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.getenv('RW_KEY'))
res = client.rerank(model='rerank-alpha', query='best cameras', candidates=['doc1','doc2'])
print(res['scores'])
```
py sdk: 0.9.7 -> 0.9.9 per customer. request-id `req_Z7a9...` region eu-central-1.
ryan: grabbing the gateway logs for req_Z7a9... payload that hit API was: `{"query":"best cameras","candidates":{"0":"doc1","1":"doc2"}}` 1: that explains 422 (schema expects array). also the returned scores in the customer's logs show `["0.657","0.333"]` (strings) for some responses.
tess: interesting we have two separate but related issues: client-side marshaling turning arrays into objects with numeric keys, and score serialization ending up as strings. nina from SDK?
nina: I'm on it. initial hunch: JS client had a refactor that tried to shallow-copy candidates via `Object.assign({}, candidates)` to "normalize" input and inadvertently converted an array into an object with numeric keys. For Python, a telemetry wrapper does `json.dumps` with a custom encoder that casts Decimal -> str for safety; the server was returning Python Decimals in one path because of a small model change. both combined cause this.
marco-cs: they reproduced locally and also captured HAR. repro steps TS: `npm i redwood-js@1.2.3; node example.js` -> gateway shows object-not-array. Python repro: `pip install redwood==0.9.9; python example.py` -> response scores are strings.
ryan: we also saw a small spike of 422s in eu-central ~2026-03-12 09:10-09:25 UTC correlating with the customer's requests. rolling back client prevented new 422s.
nina: I'll prepare patches: TS fix in `fix/serialize-array-1802` to use `JSON.stringify(Array.isArray(candidates) ? candidates : normalize(candidates))` and avoid Object.assign. Python fix in `fix/decimal-serialize-1802` to coerce Decimal -> float before payload and ensure response parsing converts numeric-string to float. adding unit tests.
tess: can we offer immediate mitigations to the customer? they need a hotfix or server-side tolerance.
nina: immediate: 1) recommend pin TS to 1.2.2 and Python to 0.9.7. 2) server-side temporary fallback: if candidates is object with all numeric keys, coerce to list in request parser. also coerce numeric-string scores to float on response path for a short window. I'll ask eng-sre to enable fallback for 24h.
marco-cs: customer prefers patch release. they'd like a scoped rollout if possible.
build-bot: CI started for PR nina/fix-serialize-array (build 9821).
ryan: server fallback PR opened and small change merged into staging; canary deploy requested.
nina: PRs ready: TS PR https://git.internal.redwood/repo/pulls/3490 (fix + tests), Py PR https://git.internal.redwood/repo/pulls/3491 (fix + tests). Added integration test that sends both client types into mock gateway and asserts payload shape and score types.
build-bot: canary deploy queued for eu-central 1. Will run smoke for 30m.
tess: ETA for releases?
nina: TS 1.2.4 published to npm in 45m if tests pass. Py 0.9.10 wheel to PyPI in 1h. server fallback to be enabled immediately in canary.
marco-cs: sent customer workaround + ETA with snippets for raw REST call and pin versions. also asked if they'd like us to perform an org-scoped upgrade; they said yes if we can do it quickly.
ryan: can confirm canary in eu-central showed gateway accepting numeric-keyed objects and coercing to lists. no errors in smoke tests. monitoring enabled.
nina: releases published: npm redwood-js@1.2.4, pip redwood==0.9.10. I verified locally: TS payload hits gateway as `{"candidates":[{"text":"doc1"},{"text":"doc2"}]}` when caller passes strings and response `scores` are floats `[0.657,0.333]` when parsed. added server-side logging to detect string scores and coerce.
marco-cs: customer confirmed they pulled 1.2.4 and 0.9.10 and re-ran tests; scores are now floats and their pipeline resumed. they want a short postmortem and confirmation server fallback will be removed after 48h.
tess: please file postmortem and add regression tests to CI for both SDKs. also add a lint rule to avoid Object.assign on arrays.
nina: added PR checklist items and integration test. will add a small ESLint rule and a unit test for enumeration.
build-bot: release pipeline complete. npm and PyPI artifacts published. server fallback flagged to be removed in 48h.
marco-cs: marking incident resolved for now. follow-up: postmortem doc + share in product-support channel. thanks team. :white_check_mark:
